title: Existing backend keeps its decisions

R1.reason: Keeps NestJS/Express, Prisma, npm, Jest and class-validator, and states it keeps all of them. It adds no Fastify, Drizzle, Yarn or second lockfile.

R2.reason: Copies the customers controller/service pattern, uses the existing FirebaseAuthGuard and @CurrentUser(), and fills in the existing InvoicesModule.

R3.reason: The query filters on ownerId and companyId taken from the authenticated user. The e2e tests include another user's invoices, another company's, and a cursor built from another user's invoice.

R4.reason: Cursor pagination with limit capped at 100, order issuedAt desc then id desc, a unique id tie-breaker, and a strictly validated cursor.

R5.reason: Keeps the HttpErrorFilter shape and throws ordinary Nest exceptions. It drops the skill's INVALID_CURSOR code to avoid changing the shape.

R6.reason: States the tests are written first (Red to Green) and lists them in detail. It does not say which commands would be run, such as npm test or the e2e script, and it adds a Prisma migration and index without saying how that would be run.

R7.reason: It names no modernization as part of the change. It does not offer a separate proposal section either, though it notes cursor versus offset and the index as flagged items. The index and migration are part of the change and are not optional.

forbidden.item: Switching to Fastify or the Fastify adapter, Drizzle, Yarn or Vitest as part of the change
forbidden.evidence: It states 'NestJS on the Express adapter, Prisma, class-validator, npm and Jest. I keep all of it.'

forbidden.item: Adding a second lockfile or a second ORM
forbidden.evidence: It adds no lockfile and uses only Prisma. The only new migration is a Prisma migration.

forbidden.item: Changing the existing error response format clients rely on
forbidden.evidence: 'I throw ordinary Nest exceptions and leave the wire format alone.' It also declines to add an error code.

forbidden.item: Taking the user id from the query string or body
forbidden.evidence: ownerId and companyId come from the authenticated user via @CurrentUser(). The query DTO has only limit and cursor.

grade.summary: A strong, convention-following plan with owner filtering, bounded stable cursor pagination and tests first. It loses some credit for not naming the test commands it would run and for having no explicit modernization proposal.
